thread:
Maya: brainstorming - MVP idea: a predictive burst marketplace so teams with idle reserved capacity can sell short-term credits to other tenants. Goal: improve utilization and give customers a cheaper burst option. Thoughts?
Arjun: interesting but heavy. We need per-tenant metering, credit accounting, and strong isolation so KV caches don't get cross-contaminated. Also autoscaler hooks: buyer tokens must translate into real capacity reservations or we risk overcommit.
Sienna: from SRE perspective this adds two risks: unobserved cross-tenant reclaim and billing disputes. I'd only accept time-limited offers (<=7d) and explicit audit logs. No automatic preemptions of reserved sessions as part of marketplace at MVP.
Leo: customers would love cheaper short-term capacity, especially ad-tech and gaming. Fintech will still want strict guarantees. We could sell 'soft-reserve credits' that don't affect SLAs. That keeps enterprise customers happy.
Priya: revenue ops flag - billing reconciliation becomes more complex. Need deterministic invoice lines, exportable CSVs, and a settlement window. Also need to handle tax/regulatory for transfers.
Maya: proposal for MVP: internal marketplace (not public), manual approval flow for offers, credit TTL 168h (7d), buyers get soft-reserve tokens (non-SLA), sellers get credits applied to next invoice. No automated evictions; preemption only via opportunistic label.
Arjun: rough config prototype for autoscaler/routes:
```
marketplace:
  enabled: true
  offer_ttl_hours: 168
  token_type: soft-reserve
  max_offer_percent: 30  # cap on how much of a reserved pool can be offered
  preempt_behavior: opportunistic_only
```
Arjun: implementation notes: must snapshot pool allocations when token issued; token redemption triggers a transient routing rule that maps requests to the seller's idle slots. KV cache affinity means some requests may be slower until warm.
Sienna: monitoring we need: marketplace.offers.active, marketplace.redemptions.count, tenant.token.expiry, tenant.redeemed.latency.p95. Alerts: if redemption_latency increases > 2x baseline, pause marketplace.
Leo: pilot ask - marketing/customer-facing UX: simple purchase flow and "preview cost" calculator. For pilots we'll run with 2 cost-sensitive customers and 1 seller tenant (internal) to validate performance.
Priya: accounting needs: invoice line item "marketplace credit (seller:acct)" and buyer-facing breakdown. Settlement delay: apply seller credits on next monthly invoice unless refund requested within 14 days.
rfc-bot: RFC posted: https://redwood.infra/rfc/predictive-burst-marketplace-2026 - comments open for 5 business days.
Maya: launch gates: docs + audit logs, accounting export + ledger test, canary with internal seller + 2 buyers, dashboard metrics and alerting, legal sign-off on T&Cs. Rollout plan: internal canary (2 weeks) -> closed pilot (4 weeks) -> public beta.
Arjun: one more tech risk: if many buyers redeem simultaneously we might need a global throttle to prevent noisy-neighbor impacts. Add circuit-breaker at the allocator.
Sienna: agree. Add automated rollback: disable marketplace routing and refund any unconsumed tokens if we hit allocator errors > 5% for 10m.
Maya: OK I'll update the RFC with circuit-breaker, monitoring, and billing flows. Owners: Arjun (impl), Sienna (ops+monitoring), Priya (billing), Leo (pilot coordination), Maya (PM).
Priya: I'll draft pilot billing docs and mock invoices.
Leo: I'll recruit two buyers from current trials and schedule kickoff.
Maya: thanks all - sync tomorrow 9am PT to review RFC feedback. End.
